chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Wuheyb ibn Hafs, from Abu Baseer, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), regarding the handshake of the Muslim with the Jew and the Christian.
He said: 'From behind a cloth. So if he shakes your hand with his hand, then wash your hand.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on shaking hands with Jews and Christians?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Shia juristic principle of maintaining ritual purity (taharah) during social interactions with People of the Book, reflecting the view that their external contact may carry a degree of impurity. The directive to shake hands 'from behind the cloth' or wash the hand upon direct contact underscores a balance between maintaining communal ties (mu'asharah) and preserving religious distinctiveness. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the boundaries of physical interaction in mixed-faith societies.
